indeterminate.checklist_item: - [ ] Make a broad non-global scope stop with a missing/None coordinate a loud error (or halt all in-scope) rather than silently matching nothing.
evidence: coordinator.py:231: `if coord is not None and coords.get(scope.value) == coord:`
coordinator.py:127-128: default `_empty_locate` returns `{}`, so `.get(scope.value)` is None

A broad endpoint failure recorded with coord=None can never match any downstream plan in _halted_diagnostic, so siblings run — the halt verdict is silent both when there is no failure and when the coordinate producer supplied nothing.
indeterminate.finding: A broad (endpoint/tenant/provider) authoritative failure silently fails to halt sibling tickets when locate() returns no coordinate for that scope key. _record_effects stores the stop as (scope, locate(...).get(scope.value)), which is None with the default _empty_locate (or any locate missing that key), and _halted_diagnostic only matches when `coord is not None`. The AC4/AC5 scope-isolation guard therefore degrades to no isolation, indistinguishable from 'no broad failure occurred'.
scenarios: coordinate() called with the default locate (None) and an adapter returning a broad endpoint/tenant/provider-scoped failure
locate provided but returning a mapping missing the failing scope's key
indeterminate.suggested_fix: When _record_effects computes a broad non-global scope stop, assert/require a non-None coordinate (raise or fall back to a conservative halt) so a missing locate coordinate cannot silently defeat the scope halt.

indeterminate.checklist_item: - [ ] Propagate the failing AtomicSignal.diagnostic into the TicketOutcome.diagnostics for executed-plan failures.
evidence: coordinator.py:67: `diagnostic: str | None = None` on AtomicSignal
coordinator.py:170-206: _run_atomic_op / _execute_plan return only (disposition, scope[, postconditions]); signal.diagnostic is never read
coordinator.py:250: `return _make_outcome(plan, disp, scope, postconditions, ())` — diagnostics always empty for the execute path
search of coordinator.py shows `signal.diagnostic` is never referenced
indeterminate.finding: AtomicSignal.diagnostic is defined but never propagated onto TicketOutcome. For executed (mutate) plans, _make_outcome is always called with an empty diagnostics tuple, so a permanent/exhausted failure carries no explanation of why it failed.
scenarios: An adapter returns AtomicSignal(status='permanent', diagnostic='stale binding 404') — the diagnostic is dropped and the failed TicketOutcome has diagnostics==()
indeterminate.suggested_fix: Thread signal.diagnostic through _run_atomic_op/_execute_plan and include it in _make_outcome's diagnostics tuple on non-success outcomes.

indeterminate.checklist_item: - [ ] Handle a None defer_reason on a non-mutate plan with a defined disposition (e.g. default to skipped) instead of raising ValueError.
evidence: failure_policy.py:133: `return Disposition(getattr(defer_reason, "value", defer_reason))` — Disposition(None) raises ValueError
ticket_plan.py:153: `defer_reason: DeferReason | None = None` (None is a valid TicketPlan state)
indeterminate.finding: _build_outcome calls defer_reason_to_disposition(plan.defer_reason) for any non-mutate plan, which raises ValueError when defer_reason is None. TicketPlan.defer_reason is typed `DeferReason | None`, so a non-mutate plan with no defer_reason (permitted by the type) crashes the whole coordination run.
scenarios: A TicketPlan with disposition 'defer'/'noop' and defer_reason=None is passed to coordinate()
indeterminate.suggested_fix: In _build_outcome, guard for plan.defer_reason is None (map to Disposition.skipped or a documented default) before calling defer_reason_to_disposition.

indeterminate.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test for a single mutate plan whose postconditions mix `applied` and `recovered` success signals, asserting the ticket disposition/bucket is `recovered` (precedence).
evidence: coordinator.py:184-191: `seen = {pc.disposition for pc in postconditions}` then `if Disposition.recovered in seen: return Disposition.recovered` / `if Disposition.applied in seen: return Disposition.applied`

Violating input: a plan with mutations [update→AtomicSignal(status='applied'), delete→AtomicSignal(status='recovered')] should yield ticket disposition `recovered` (recovered bucket); no test constructs such a plan. `test_recovered_op_is_recovered_bucket` uses a single recovered op only.

ABSENCE: no test in test_operation_coordinator.py scripts two success signals of differing precedence on one plan; a regression collapsing the precedence (e.g. returning `applied` whenever `applied` is present, or dropping the recovered check) would go undetected.
indeterminate.finding: The `_combine_success` recovered-over-applied precedence is untested: no test drives a single mutate plan with multiple SUCCESS postconditions mixing `applied` and `recovered` to verify the combined ticket disposition resolves to `recovered`. Only a single-op recovered plan is tested (`test_recovered_op_is_recovered_bucket`), and the only multi-postcondition test (`test_late_failure_preserves_earlier_postcondition_and_never_replays`) mixes applied+permanent on the failure path.
